descriptions.text: Alarm Module. Two items for the price of one! A favorite of the paranoid and the rich, you can use this module to either add an alarm element to a trap you're building, or it can be used as a ready-to-go trap for those who can't be assed to sit down and make their own. When triggered, it will play a Very Loud song. And by Very Loud, I mean Norwegian Black Metal loud. You may program the song at a Sapper's Table. If you do not or are unable to pick an alarm tone, a random, culturally-important song from the past US Billboard Hot 100 will be chosen. …

beats.headline: Two trap modules
beats.text: Back in the safe room after the battle, Donut opens her loot boxes. The only new thing is two Trap Modules from her gold sapper's box: one called a Spike Module and the other an Alarm Module. These are ready-to-go traps, no tinkering required. They can be upgraded and reconfigured, but only with a sapper's table.

beats.headline: A song in the gangway
beats.text: Rabid babies are at both doors of the car when Carl asks Donut whether she still has those two trap modules. Each is a tiny cube about the size of a pair of dice. He sets the alarm on the floor of the fore gangway and puts the spike module on the janitor car's door. When the babies break through, the announcement rattles the walls: peaking at number 2 on January 13, 2007, it's Fergalicious. Donut loves this song.

beats.headline: Physical, through the portal
beats.text: The carts make hardly any noise, which is a problem for the crawlers waiting at the far end of the line, so Carl puts an alarm trap on each of the six: thirty-minute delays on five, one minute on the last, to make sure the delay works before it goes through the portal. Donut is sure it will be Wonderwall. Peaking at Number 1 on Nov 16, 1981, it's Physical, so loud Carl takes a small amount of damage. He pushes the throttle, jumps down, and watches it shoot down the track into the portal.

beats.headline: Bouncing to the beat
beats.text: Carl made five of these at his sapper's table, each labelled with a purpose, and because he built them there he could pick the songs. This one says Bass heavy. For distraction: a hollow banger sphere with an impact-detonated alarm trap inside. Katia lobs it down the stairs at the ooze. Peaking at Number 2 on October 10th, 1992, it's Jump Around. Muffled by the metal, it still shakes the walls, and the ball bounces with the beat, slipping out of the ooze's grasp. Donut asks if that is seriously the only bass-heavy song he could think of.

beats.headline: Swallowed by a shark
beats.text: In the water the party is sandwiched between the current and a mob, apparently a shark, lazily circling toward them. The creature crunches on a corpse and some other debris, and when it opens its mouth Carl can hear the distinctive beat of Jump Around blast out into the ocean. It has eaten the goddamned alarm trap. None of Carl's explosives with exposed fuses will work well under water, and he is not keen to be anywhere near the ones that might.

beats.headline: Donut picks the song
beats.text: Invisible, Carl chucks an alarm ball as hard as he can toward the club's front entrance. He has no idea what the song will be: Donut begged to pick a few for the distraction balls, and he let her, for the practice at his sapper's table. Topping at number two on March 23rd, 1985, it's Material Girl. As the Madonna song starts and the large demon turns toward the music, Carl bolts across the open space, and the body of a dead sai she has just tossed away slams him through the doors into the kitchens.
